text:
Calgary spent most of the night as the better team and finally had the scoreboard say so in the last four minutes. Martin Pospisil's goal at 15:38 of the third put CGY ahead 3-2, and Yegor Sharangovich sealed the 4-2 win at 18:38 with a wrist shot on an 87% chance. The third period was lopsided in expected goals, 2.33 for CGY against 0.92 for ANA, so the late goals were closer to a correction than a surprise.

The first period set the tone. Adam Klapka opened the scoring at 8:32 on a 3% snap shot, the least likely goal of the game. ANA answered twice, Beckett Sennecke tying it at 12:09 and Leo Carlsson putting the home side up 2-1 on the power play at 14:05, even though CGY led the period 1.58 to 0.81 in expected goals. Aydar Suniev tied it at 8:02 of the second, one of the few stretches where ANA had the better chances (1.24 to 1.01).

Over the full game, CGY finished with 4.91 expected goals to ANA's 2.97 and 73 shot attempts to 65. That gave CGY a 61% share of simulated replays, against 39% for ANA. Dustin Wolf saved 0.97 goals more than his 25 shots deserved, while Lukas Dostal held ANA in it, stopping 32 of 35. Sennecke was named first star for the home side, but ANA lost the second meeting between these teams in four days after winning the first 4-2.
